submitter: provocation_pipeline lane (working in gauntlet_dead_cta's code at owner instruction)
rationale: RFC_020 §5.2, authorised by the owner on 2026-08-10 after he raised a liability brief: low risk appetite, keep the viral effect. The Gauntlet publishes a visitor's prose AND an AI verdict at a permanent public URL. The finding that shaped this: publishing is an AMPLIFIER, not a threshold — communicating a statement about a named third party to one person is already publication — so the control has to target the harm rather than the duration, which is why a timed URL was recommended against and this was recommended instead. The design decision worth challenging is that this is NOT a name detector. On the ruled audience (food, music and film canon, cities, generational habits — PLAN §11.1) naming things IS the argument, so refusing anything that names a real person would refuse the product and buy nothing: 'Christopher Nolan is overrated' is opinion. What creates exposure is a NAMED ENTITY plus a CHECKABLE ALLEGATION about it — 'Nolan stole the script'. That is the same thesis/assertion split the provocation gate already makes. This is layer A only: deterministic, no model, no network call, therefore unable to fail open; a model layer is the natural layer B and is explicitly not claimed here. Note this edits another lane's service (internal/tools-api, gauntlet_dead_cta's) at the owner's explicit instruction, and they have been told in their cold-start INCOMING.

plan.summary: A deterministic publish-time gate that refuses to make a Gauntlet round public when it makes a checkable allegation about an apparently-named third party. Detection is driven from the allegation term outward to nearby names, not from names inward, which is what makes it usable on a product where naming things is the point. Checks the model's own output on the same terms as the visitor's. Fails closed.

edits.symbol: Scan, ScanAll, allegationOccurrences, nameNear, opensSentence, allegationTerms, standaloneTerms
edits.rationale: New package rather than a handler helper because it is the whole judgement and needs its own tests; it has no dependencies beyond regexp/strings/utf8 so it cannot fail open on a network or model error. THE LOOP DIRECTION IS THE DESIGN AND IT IS WHAT I MOST WANT REVIEWED: it iterates allegation terms and looks for a name nearby, NOT the reverse. The first version ran the other way and was wrong twice in ways the tests caught — a name OPENING a sentence was discarded along with 'The Guardian…', so 'Christopher Nolan stole the script' passed; and single-word names were never matched, so 'Nolan plagiarised it' passed. Both are precisely the target case. Inverting also shrinks the false-positive surface for free, because capitalised tokens are only ever inspected near an allegation, so ordinary naming is never examined. allegationTerms deliberately excludes quality words (overrated, boring, derivative, terrible) — a site built for argument must permit them.

edits.symbol: 7 tests incl. TestOpinionAboutNamedThingsIsALLOWED and a mutation control
edits.rationale: The load-bearing test is the PRODUCT one, not the risk one: eight real opinions about named things ('The Beatles are the most boring band ever canonised', 'New York is a worse city than Chicago') must all pass, because if they do not the feature is dead and the gate has cost more than it saved. Paired with the risk set that must all be refused. TestTheProximityTestsWouldCatchTheWindowBeingRemoved is a can-fail control asserting the windowed and unwindowed variants genuinely differ on the far case, so the proximity test cannot pass by accident. Two tests were CORRECTED during the run rather than the code being bent to them — recorded in the test file itself: I had asserted 'The Guardian lied about the numbers.' should be ALLOWED, and the code was right to refuse it.

The gate runs at PublishHandler because that is the ONLY place a round stops being one person's private argument and becomes a permanent public record — playing, scoring and reading your own round are untouched, so the visitor loses only the share link. BOTH halves are scanned: round.Counter and round.Verdict are the SERVICE's text, which per RFC_020 §1.4 makes them the part we are most clearly the author of, not the least. Fails closed on a read error. The site-scope check is a fix for a leak the gate itself would otherwise INTRODUCE: store.GetRound is not site-scoped (PublishRound is), so without it a cross-site round_id could answer 422 instead of 404, distinguishing 'exists on another site AND contains an allegation' from everything else.

Logs the refusal as a SHAPE — Kind and Term from the package's own closed vocabulary — and deliberately NOT Finding.Match, which holds the apparent third-party name lifted from the visitor's prose. Logging that would write the identified person's name into our logs, creating a durable record of exactly what the refusal exists to avoid publishing. Same reasoning and same owner ruling (2026-07-27) as logAIBadResponse's fingerprint, which replaced a capped excerpt for this reason. The refusal reasons are also NOT returned to the caller: a caller who could see which term tripped it could tune prose against the check until it passed.

grounded_in: OWNER BRIEF 2026-08-09: 'someone can say something insulting about someone and then it gets validated by the site and posted over the internet. I may be liable … I still want the viral effect somehow but my risk appetite is low.' Then 2026-08-10, authorising this: 'please go ahead as you suggest.'

architecture_review/RFC_020 §1.2 — publication for defamation is communication to one person other than the subject, so the public URL amplifies reach and damages rather than creating the exposure. This is why the control targets content rather than duration, and why RFC_020 §5.6 recommends AGAINST the timed URL the owner originally suggested.

architecture_review/RFC_020 §1.4 — the verdict is the service's own text, not user-generated content, which is why namecheck.ScanAll covers round.Counter and round.Verdict and not only the visitor's prose.

PLAN_2026-07-31_provocation_pipeline.md §11.1 (owner ruling 2026-08-09) — the audience is everyday culture orthodoxies: food, music and film canon, cities, generational habits. This is the measurement behind 'a name detector would refuse the product': on that audience, naming things IS the argument.

internal/tools-api/handlers/ailog.go:73-88 — logAIBadResponse 'records the response's SHAPE, never its text … the owner ruled for a fingerprint on 2026-07-27'. logPublishRefusal follows the same rule for the same reason; Finding.Match is excluded on that precedent.

internal/tools-api/store/rounds.go:54 — GetRound takes (ctx, pool, roundID) with NO site_id predicate, while PublishRound (:191) is site-scoped. That asymmetry is the reason for the explicit round.SiteID != siteID check; publish.go's own existing comment already notes position/defend share the unscoped shape.

internal/tools-api/store/rounds.go:19-27 — Round carries PositionText, DefenceText, Counter and Verdict, so no new store function was needed; the gate reuses the existing loader rather than adding a second read path that could drift.

bugs_open/232 — the same public round URL is search-engine indexable; fixed separately by another session (c3d7841f9, pages.noindex + X-Robots-Tag). Named here because the two controls are complementary: 232 reduces discoverability, this reduces what exists to discover. Neither substitutes for the other.

Test evidence, this change: 7 tests, all executing and green (`go test ./internal/tools-api/namecheck/ -v`), and the full service suite green (`go test ./internal/tools-api/...`). Two test EXPECTATIONS were corrected during the run rather than the code being bent to fit them, and the corrections are recorded in the test file's own comments.
plan.risks: (1) FALSE POSITIVES ARE THE PRODUCT RISK AND THEY ARE NOT MEASURED AGAINST REAL TRAFFIC. The eight-opinion allow-set is my own composition, not a sample of visitor prose — and a fixture I compose to exercise a rule will tend to exercise it. There is no real corpus to test against because only our own harness rounds exist. This is the weakest part of the change and the honest way to fix it is to measure refusals once traffic exists, via logPublishRefusal's signals, not to argue about it now. (2) FALSE NEGATIVES ARE CERTAIN: this is a word-list layer, so paraphrase, misspelling and implication all defeat it. It is deliberately layer A of the provocation gate's A/B/C shape and does not claim to be the control. Stated in the package doc comment so no later reader mistakes nil for 'safe'. (3) ENGLISH ONLY, and the capitalisation heuristic assumes a script that has case — it will under-detect on anything else. (4) THE STANDALONE TERM LIST IS A BLUNT INSTRUMENT: 'grooming' has an innocent sense (grooming a dog, grooming a successor) and will refuse those shares. Accepted deliberately — a false positive costs one visitor a share button, and this is the category where a false negative is worst. (5) NOT LIVE ON COMMIT: tools-api ships from the island VM (docker compose, scp), not the chassis, so this is inert until that deploy — which is the gauntlet lane's, and deliberately not done unasked. (6) THIS EDITS ANOTHER LANE'S SERVICE, at the owner's instruction. Their cold-start carries an INCOMING block. (7) NOT COVERED, and both are open RFC_020 items: §5.3 (a published report/takedown route) and §5.4 (making the verdict's scope explicit in the artefact) are not in this change.
